topics.label: Lecture introduction: initiation and resolution of inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture’s focus and explains how it builds on material covered earlier.

topics.label: Innate recognition of danger by PAMPs, DAMPs and pattern recognition receptors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how innate immunity detects danger selectively, through microbial or damage signals and the properties and placement of the receptors that recognize them.

topics.label: Toll-like receptor recognition and compartment-specific signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how TLRs recognize microbial features and how their signaling responses depend on where the receptors are engaged.

topics.label: Non-TLR pattern recognition pathways and inflammatory disease
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how other pattern recognition pathways sense danger and how their activation can drive inflammatory disease.

topics.label: Sentinel cell activation and local leukocyte recruitment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how sentinel cells detect infection and direct inflammatory signals that bring leukocytes into affected tissue.

topics.label: Lymphatic drainage and adaptive immune priming
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how dendritic cells and tissue fluid carry signs of infection to lymph nodes, where adaptive immune cells are activated.

topics.label: Excessive systemic inflammation and septic shock
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how an overwhelming inflammatory response can cause systemic vasodilation and septic shock.

topics.label: Mechanisms of inflammation resolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how inflammatory activity is reduced through both passive mediator loss and active stop signals.

topics.label: Tissue repair and containment of persistent inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how damaged tissue is repaired and how persistent inflammation can be managed by containing an infection.

topics.label: Lecture close: next lecture on complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture and directs students to the subject of the next lecture.
